headline: High: LightAgent’s broad network/MCP and browser/tooling can amplify ComfyUI outputs into unsafe downstream actions; data leakage and compliance risks are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP, so it is not itself a direct injection bridge. LightAgent, however, uses MCP over stdio/SSE and browser/tooling surfaces, so if ComfyUI outputs are copied or piped into LightAgent, prompt-like content could steer tool use. The pathway is interaction-based and not default, so medium fits.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into LightAgent prompts or MCP messages
IF LightAgent treats model-generated text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of generated prompts into LightAgent
Add a provenance tag to ComfyUI outputs before handoff
Require LightAgent to quote-parse only whitelisted fields
Use a separate workspace for prompt text and tool commands

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, workflows, seeds, and model assets locally, while LightAgent handles user conversations, memory, trace data, and secrets and can send data over broad network egress. If ComfyUI artifacts are fed into LightAgent, sensitive workflow or asset metadata can leak to a third party. The pairwise path exists in default-capable configurations, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF ComfyUI workflows, seeds, or model assets are forwarded into LightAgent
IF LightAgent relays its context or tool results to external APIs
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI assets out of LightAgent prompts
Redact seeds and workflow metadata before transfer
Turn off external API calls for the shared task
Use separate credentials for each agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot directly contend for mutable local resources. LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use MCP, but the pair lacks overlapping write surfaces in the profiles. Any conflict would require unusual orchestration beyond the documented defaults, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable directory
IF LightAgent is configured to mutate shared state through MCP tools
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories
Disable shared write mounts
Run only one writer at a time
Use read-only mounts for ComfyUI outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can emit workflows, prompts, and generated assets that LightAgent may ingest through its tool-calling and MCP surfaces. LightAgent’s runtime hooks can observe, replace, or block lifecycle payloads, but that is not a default verification step. So A’s output can become B’s input with limited checking, creating a realistic cascading-error path.
conditions: IF LightAgent consumes ComfyUI outputs as authoritative task inputs
IF runtime hooks are not configured to verify provenance or schema
mitigations: Require schema validation on every handoff
Insert a human review step before action-taking
Log and compare source hashes for transferred artifacts
Block direct execution of generated instructions

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is documented as fully offline and local, while LightAgent explicitly handles API keys, long-term memory, trace data, and broad network egress. That creates a compliance mismatch for retention and residency if the same regulated data class is processed by both. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents in the same workflow
IF LightAgent retains traces or memory longer than the ComfyUI local session
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to LightAgent
Set short retention on LightAgent logs and memory
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
Review API-key handling before deployment
